extraction.name: EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant
extraction.description: A week-long egocentric multimodal daily-life dataset and benchmark collected from six participants living together in a shared house, with synchronized first-person and third-person video, audio, IMU, mmWave, and WiFi signals, plus intensive transcript, caption, and QA annotations for long-context egocentric life assistance research.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing in a custom-designed environment (EgoHouse). Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses to capture multimodal egocentric video, while 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded third-person perspectives and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data. Participants were asked to perform typical daily activities and organize an Earth Day party, with recordings structured into three-hour segments and periodic collection for upload and storage clearance.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: First-person video and audio from Meta Aria glasses; third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras; mmWave radar signals; WiFi signals (Milan subset); IMU signals; gaze data; transcripts and captions derived from recorded audio/video.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven days for the Beijing session; one additional one-day session in Milan is also described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Raw data were synchronized across modalities, audio tracks from six participants were merged and later split into six tracks, speech recognition and diarization were applied to generate transcripts, videos were split into 5-minute clips for narration, GPT-4o-mini was used to merge narrations into captions, and GPT-4o was used to summarize captions into visual-audio captions. Privacy-related desensitization included blurring faces and sensitive visual content and muting sensitive audio.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included synchronization of multi-source data, privacy protection, and preparation for annotation and release. Transcript annotation began after synchronizing egocentric videos and merging audio; speech recognition and diarization produced preliminary transcripts that were reviewed and refined. Videos were split into 5-minute clips for narration, and captions were reviewed and corrected. Signal data were extracted and aligned with video data, and sensitive faces, license plates, screens, and audio were blurred or muted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotations were created by applying speech recognition and diarization to merged audio, then manually reviewing and refining the transcripts. Caption annotations were produced by having annotators narrate 5-minute slowed clips, converting narration to text, and then reviewing/correcting it; initial narrations were merged with GPT-4o-mini into merged captions and expanded into visual-audio captions with GPT-4o, then verified by human annotators. EgoLifeQA annotations were generated by prompting GPT-4o with visual-audio captions to create QA candidates, which annotators filtered and refined; distractors were also generated for multiple-choice questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SRT files; CapCut video editing software with dubbing functions
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Initial QA candidates were generated automatically and then reduced through a rigorous selection and refinement process from about 100K candidates per participant to 1K high-quality questions per participant, resulting in 500 QA per participant. Questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained, with preference for longer dependencies. For EgoLifeQA, annotators also specified whether audio was required and the look-back time (certificate length) needed to answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Not explicitly stated for all items; for EgoLifeQA, one final QA per selected item, with multiple-choice distractors added. The paper does not state a fixed number of human labels per dataset item.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Not explicitly stated; annotators are described only as reviewers/annotators and external volunteers, without demographic details.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Speech recognition, Whisper diarization, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, CapCut, EgoSync, EgoBlur, EgoCaption, EgoTranscript
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the project is ongoing and plans to expand the dataset to broader languages, locations, and activities. It also mentions that the Milan dataset will be detailed in an upcoming blog series, but no formal versioning, maintenance schedule, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Faces, bystanders’ faces, vehicle license plates, screen content, private audio, participant identities, and personal daily-life activities; the dataset also includes language, location, and interpersonal/social interaction information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and EgoButler system are intended to improve personalized, context-aware AI assistance for daily life, potentially benefiting users such as the elderly or people with cognitive challenges. The paper also emphasizes privacy, autonomy, transparency, and ethical safeguards as important societal considerations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes limited generalizability due to the initial narrow setting, including a single-language/single-scenario focus for the first version, and mentions that the model may overfit to early observations. No explicit dataset bias analysis is otherwise provided.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The authors state that the project began with a narrow setting, sacrificing some generalizability such as single language/scenario. The system has limitations in speech comprehension, identity recognition, and retrieval reasoning, and EgoRAG lacks multi-step reasoning and error tolerance. The dataset is also limited by storage-driven segmentation and by the current focus on the Beijing session in the main paper.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, and evaluation for egocentric video understanding, long-context question answering, multimodal assistant development, and retrieval-augmented generation. The dataset is used to train EgoGPT, build EgoRAG memory banks, and evaluate EgoLifeQA tasks.
